title: N8N Docker Restart Causes API Key Invalidation (v1.7.3 Incident)
executive_summary: During v1.7.3 milestone work to fix WEBHOOK_URL environment variable, we restarted the n8n Docker container without proper credential persistence strategy. This invalidated the N8N_API_KEY stored in ~/.zshrc, causing 401 Unauthorized errors for all API calls. The incident revealed a critical gap in our operational procedures: no backup/restore strategy for n8n credentials during infrastructure changes.

incident_timeline.event: Discovered WEBHOOK_URL was null in n8n container
incident_timeline.action: Decided to restart Docker container with correct environment variables

incident_timeline.event: Executed: docker stop <old-container> && docker run -d --name n8n -e WEBHOOK_URL=... n8nio/n8n:latest
incident_timeline.action: Container restarted successfully with WEBHOOK_URL set

incident_timeline.event: Attempted to re-validate workflows via n8n API

incident_timeline.diagnosis: Docker restart invalidated API key without proper persistence

incident_timeline.action: Automated future recovery from this failure pattern

root_cause_analysis.primary_cause: Docker container restart without credential persistence strategy
contributing_factors: Prioritized speed (fixing WEBHOOK_URL) over safety (backup credentials)
Assumed ~/.n8n volume mount would preserve all state including API keys
No documented procedure for safe n8n container restarts
No pre-restart checklist (backup API key, export workflows, verify volume mounts)
root_cause_analysis.why_it_happened: When docker run creates a new container, n8n generates new internal encryption keys for its SQLite database. Even though the ~/.n8n volume was mounted, the API keys are encrypted with instance-specific keys that changed on restart.

technical_details.command_executed: docker run -d --name n8n --restart always -p 5678:5678 -e WEBHOOK_URL="https://n8n.pbradygeorgen.com" -e N8N_PROTOCOL="https" -e N8N_HOST="n8n.pbradygeorgen.com" -e N8N_PORT="5678" -e N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL="https://n8n.pbradygeorgen.com" -v ~/.n8n:/home/node/.n8n n8nio/n8n:latest
technical_details.volume_contents: SQLite database (encrypted), workflow JSONs, credential JSONs, user settings
technical_details.api_key_storage: Encrypted in SQLite database with instance-specific encryption key
technical_details.encryption_key_location: Generated on container first boot, stored in container memory
technical_details.why_api_key_invalidated: New container = new encryption key = cannot decrypt old API keys

symptoms.ui_behavior: n8n UI is accessible and shows workflows, but API key from ~/.zshrc doesn't work

recovery_procedure.time_to_recovery: 5-10 minutes (if workflows preserved), 15-20 minutes (if workflows lost)
recovery_procedure.data_loss_risk: LOW if ~/.n8n volume mounted correctly, HIGH if volume was empty/unmounted

prevention_strategies.implementation: Before ANY docker stop/restart, run: scripts/backup-n8n-state.sh
prevention_strategies.includes: Export API key, export all workflows, backup ~/.n8n directory, snapshot credentials

prevention_strategies.implementation: Store all environment variables in /opt/n8n/.env file, use docker run --env-file
prevention_strategies.benefit: Declarative configuration, git-versionable, no manual docker run commands
Prevents future incidents, provides reference for team members

prevention_strategies.implementation: Use Terraform/CloudFormation to manage EC2 + n8n with proper state persistence
prevention_strategies.benefit: Reproducible infrastructure, no manual commands, version-controlled

prevention_strategies.implementation: Cron job that tests n8n API every 5 minutes, alerts on 401
prevention_strategies.benefit: Immediate detection of API key invalidation

lessons_learned.lesson: Speed without safety creates technical debt
lessons_learned.elaboration: We prioritized fixing WEBHOOK_URL quickly without considering credential persistence. This saved 10 minutes but cost 30 minutes in recovery.
lessons_learned.future_action: Always run pre-change checklists, even if they slow us down

lessons_learned.lesson: Docker volumes don't preserve encrypted state across container recreations
lessons_learned.elaboration: Even though ~/.n8n was mounted, the encryption keys changed, making API keys unreadable.
lessons_learned.future_action: Export API keys to ~/.zshrc BEFORE container restarts

lessons_learned.lesson: Automation should include recovery procedures, not just happy paths
lessons_learned.elaboration: We automated workflow creation but not recovery from common failures.
lessons_learned.future_action: Build recovery automation alongside feature automation

lessons_learned.lesson: 401 Unauthorized is a symptom, not a root cause
lessons_learned.elaboration: We initially thought ~/.zshrc configs were wrong. Actually, the API key was simply invalidated by the restart.
lessons_learned.future_action: Investigate infrastructure changes first when credentials suddenly fail

crew_insights.commander_picard: We have successfully set the WEBHOOK_URL environment variable, but in doing so, we restarted the n8n Docker container. This restart has invalidated our API key. The n8n instance is now a FRESH installation with NEW credentials. Our ~/.zshrc N8N_API_KEY is now obsolete.
crew_insights.commander_data: When we ran 'docker run -d --name n8n -v ~/.n8n:/home/node/.n8n n8nio/n8n:latest', we mounted the ~/.n8n volume, which SHOULD have preserved workflows, credentials, API keys, and user accounts. However, the 401 Unauthorized suggests the API key was encrypted with a different key than the new container is using.
crew_insights.chief_obrien: This is what happens when you touch the metal without a full backup! We fixed the WEBHOOK_URL, but we may have lost our workflows in the process. Sometimes you just need to accept that metal work has risks.
crew_insights.lt_cmdr_la_forge: For v2.0, we should rebuild the instance with proper Infrastructure as Code (Terraform). Then we can version-control the entire stack and avoid these manual operations.
crew_insights.lt_worf: The 401 Unauthorized is n8n's security working CORRECTLY. Our old API key should NOT work after a container restart without proper credential persistence. This is NOT a bug. This is proper security hygiene.
crew_insights.dr_crusher: The patient (n8n) is ALIVE but has AMNESIA. Container running, environment variables set, but API authentication failing. Diagnosis: Identity Crisis. Prognosis: If workflows exist, EXCELLENT (just need new API key). If workflows lost, CRITICAL (need full re-import).
